title: JSON breakout in Slack/Teams notifications via backslash in import-derived title
rationale: Root cause: `backend/application/notifications/services/send_notifications_base.py:43` (MS Teams) and `:65-66` (Slack) build the webhook payload by HTML-autoescaping untrusted values into a hand-written JSON template and then string-replacing `"`→`\"` (and `'`→`\'`). HTML autoescape does not touch backslashes or control characters, so a value like `foo\` renders a literal trailing backslash; the post-render replace then turns the intended closing `"` into `\"`, breaking JSON string parity and letting an import-derived `observation.title` inject arbitrary JSON keys into the Slack/Teams message. A global post-render backslash-escape cannot fix this because the templates themselves contain literal `\n` JSON escape sequences that such a pass would corrupt — escaping must happen per variable, which is exactly what `|escapejs` does. `escapejs` emits `\uXXXX` escapes (including for `\`, `"`, `'`, `<`, `>` and control chars), which are valid inside a JSON string and cannot terminate it. The fix applies `|escapejs` to every `{{ variable }}` substituted inside a JSON string literal in all 9 Slack/MS Teams templates and removes the now-redundant `.replace()` post-processing in the two sink functions. Email templates are excluded: they are `{% autoescape off %}` plaintext, not JSON.
variants_checked: send_notifications_base.py:send_msteams_notification (line 43 sink), send_notifications_base.py:send_slack_notification (lines 65-66 sink). Callers passing untrusted data into these sinks: send_notifications_observation.py:_send_observation_notifications, send_notifications_observation_title.py (observation title path), send_notifications.py (exception/security-gate/task paths). Template variant hunt over templates/slack_*.tpl and templates/msteams_*.tpl — all 9 JSON templates (slack_observation, slack_observation_title, slack_exception, slack_task_exception, slack_product_security_gate, msteams_observation, msteams_observation_title, msteams_exception, msteams_task_exception, msteams_product_security_gate) carry the same hand-built-JSON pattern and are all patched. The 5 email_*.tpl are plaintext (`autoescape off`) and intentionally not changed.
bypass_considered: Step-5 input I tried against the original `.replace`-based code: a title ending in a backslash, `evil\` followed by `", "extra":"x`, so autoescape leaves the backslash raw and the `"`→`\"` replace produces `evil\\"` only for the data quote while the template's own closing quote becomes `evil\"...` — parity broken, JSON injection. Against an alternative "only escape backslashes post-render" fix I rejected, the bypass is the template's legitimate `\n` separators being doubled to `\\n`, silently corrupting every message — i.e. that fix is at the wrong layer. With `|escapejs` the backslash itself becomes `\u005C` and the quote `\u0022`, so neither a trailing backslash nor an embedded quote/newline/control char can reach the JSON-structure layer; the only remaining injection surface would be a template variable placed outside a string literal, and none exists in these templates.
test_note: Added `test_create_notification_message_backslash_breakout` to `backend/unittests/notifications/services/test_send_notifications_base.py` (alongside the existing `_create_notification_message` tests). It renders `msteams_observation.tpl` with a backslash-bearing title and asserts the rendered payload parses as valid JSON via `json.loads` and that the injected `extra` key is not promoted into the structure. Before the fix the trailing backslash breaks string parity and `json.loads` raises (test fails); after the fix `escapejs` neutralizes the backslash and the payload parses (test passes). Note: this test exercises `observation_1` from the project's `BaseTestCase` fixture; if that fixture object is not mutable as written, the assignment line may need to target the fixture's actual title attribute — the rendering/`json.loads` assertion is the load-bearing part.
review_reason: All hunks lie on the fix path: the two JSON-webhook sender functions at send_notifications_base.py:43 and :65-66, the 10 .tpl templates they render via `_create_notification_message`/`render_to_string` (base.py uses DjangoTemplates with default HTML autoescape, so untrusted vars were only HTML-escaped), and the unit test for those functions. The diff is a root-cause fix: it replaces the incomplete ad-hoc `.replace(""",'\\"')`/`.replace("'",...)` back-conversion — which never neutralized a literal backslash and thus allowed the `evil\", "extra":"x` JSON-string breakout the new test exercises — with `|escapejs` applied at every interpolation point, which encodes `"`, `'`, `\`, `<`, `>`, `&` as `\uXXXX` and is valid inside JSON strings; removing the now-dead `.replace` lines is correct cleanup, not suppression. No new input is trusted and no validation is weakened (escapejs is strictly stronger and now also covers previously-unprotected title/uri fields); deducting points only for the fragile final assertion in the added test, which is test-only.
